elements.element: Cap is mutual (applies to each party)
elements.evidence: "Each party's liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of"

elements.element: Cap limb (a): fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim
elements.evidence: "the fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"

elements.element: Cap limb (b): USD 1,000,000, applied as a greater-of

elements.evidence: "In no event shall either party be liable to the other for ... any special, indirect or consequential damages" (existing text retained)

elements.element: Uncapped carve-out: breach of confidentiality obligations
elements.evidence: "This cap shall not apply to a party's breach of its confidentiality ... obligations"

elements.element: Uncapped carve-out: infringement of the other party's IP
elements.evidence: "its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights"

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes
elements.evidence: "Customer's payment obligations are not damages for the purposes of this cap"

elements.element: Mutual cap of 12 months' fees (fallback cap formulation)
elements.evidence: "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000" — a greater-of cap, not a cap equal to 12 months' fees

elements.element: Fallback carve-outs: indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct
elements.evidence: "its confidentiality ... obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct"

reasons: The locked preferred level is fully satisfied: mutual greater-of cap with the exact fee basis (paid or payable, 12 months preceding the claim) plus the USD 1,000,000 floor, the retained mutual indirect/consequential exclusion, all eight required uncapped carve-outs, and the payment-obligations-are-not-damages statement.

satisfies_fallback is recorded false only on a literal reading (the fallback specifies a cap of 12 months' fees, which a greater-of formulation is not); this is immaterial because the preferred bargain is met in full and the greater-of is the customer-favourable position.

Minimality holds: a single discrete sentence pair was inserted after p0105 to supply an absent monetary cap and carve-out set; no existing sentence, the Sections 13/14 carve-out, or the risk-allocation recital was rewritten, and no new exception was introduced.

Intent preserved: all untouched commercial terms remain effective and the existing exclusive-remedy/consequential-damages architecture is unchanged; note only that "Customer" should match the defined party label used elsewhere in the agreement (the document otherwise speaks of "either party" and "Garman") to avoid an undefined term.
